suspect_instances.justification: design_brief.md documents a single clocking discipline in which every state element in access_ctrl_top is instantiated as DFF_POSEDGE, sampling on the rising edge of clk. Cross-referencing access_ctrl_netlist.v shows that u_req_ff, u_key_reg0 through u_key_reg7, u_cmp_ff, and u_out_ff are all correctly instantiated as DFF_POSEDGE, but the instance u_grant_ff is instantiated as DFF_NEGEDGE, capturing its .d input on the falling edge of clk instead of the rising edge. The .d port of u_grant_ff is tied to the net grant_pre, which is the direct output of the comparator AND2 gate u_and_final and represents the raw, unregistered access-permission decision produced by the XOR2/INV/AND2 comparison tree against REF_KEY. Because u_grant_ff samples grant_pre a half clock period earlier than the documented posedge discipline would dictate, it can latch a stale or transitional value of the comparator output before the rest of the posedge-synchronous pipeline (in particular u_cmp_ff, which samples the same grant_pre net on the correct rising edge) has settled, opening a timing window through which an incorrect permission value can propagate via grant_q and u_out_and into the registered grant_out output.

summary: A single DFF_NEGEDGE substitution was found on instance u_grant_ff, which samples the access-permission comparator output grant_pre on the falling edge of clk instead of the rising edge used by every other documented state element, violating the single posedge clocking discipline specified in design_brief.md and creating a half-cycle window for a stale grant_pre value to reach grant_out.
